newsitem.title: GERMANY: GOLF-LANGER SEEKS THIRD WIN IN A MONTH.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LANGER SEEKS THIRD WIN IN A MONTH.

text.p: Bernhard Langer chases his third title in a month and his third career victory at Gut Kaden in Hamburg in the European Tournament Players Championship (TPC) this week.

As well as trying to add to his back-to-back triumphs in the Italian Open and Benson and Hedges International, Langer also seeks to build on past successes at Gut Kaden, where he won the tournament when it was the Honda Open in 1992 and then the first TPC of Europe in 1995.
Langer did not win on the European Tour last year, his first year without a victory since 1979 in a record 16-year run.

But he made up for that with his two successes this month, which lifted him to the top of the European Order of Merit though he dropped to second behind British PGA winner Ian Woosnam on Monday when he tied for 32nd place.
To regain the lead, Langer will have to take the 125,000 pounds ($204,000) first prize in the tournament. Success would be his 10th European Tour title in his home country.
He could come under threat from Ireland's in-form Darren Clarke, who ensured himself a Ryder Cup place at Valderrama in September by taking a share of second place in the PGA on Monday.
While Clarke and Langer warm up for the U.S. Open in two weeks, reigning European number one Colin Montgomerie withdrew from Hamburg on Tuesday morning "for personal reasons".
But European Ryder Cup captain Seve Ballesteros will play despite pulling out of the PGA on Friday with a recurring back injury.
